[...]其の飲食を量って多からず少なからず、其の睡眠を調えて節せず、恋にせず」。「五どようこ観の偈」にも、「正に良薬を事とするは形枯を療ぜんが為なり」とあるが、飲食を薬だと思えば、時間を定め分量を定めて頂かねばならぬ。元来、仏戒では非時食戒といって、間食はもとより許されない。正午を過ぎたら翌朝まで、一切食事をとらんことになっておる。液体はいいが固形物は些細なものでも食べんのが原則である。ビルマやタイなど南方の僧は皆これを厳守しているが、老僧が若いころ随いておった河口慧海老人も一生これを守っておられた。坐禅は、夜間が最も心が静まって、静慮に適し三昧を得やすいのであるが、午後食事をとると血脈が乱れ、睡気を催し、三昧境に入り難くなるからである。 また、坐禅にとりかかるには、「閑静処」といって静かなところがよい。坐禅せば四条五条の橋の上往来の人を深山木に見てと、大灯国師は歌っておられるが、それは、よほど修行の進んだ達人にしてできることで、初心の者にはできんことである。「外、一切善悪の境界に於いて心念起こらず」というわけにはゆくまい。まず静かな場所を選んで、なるべく厚い座布団を敷いて、長時間堪えられる用意をするがよい。着物や帯は窮屈にならんようにゆったりと着て、しかもだらけぬように、威儀整然として、一分の隙もない気構えが必要である。 沢木興道和尚が自叙伝の中に書いておられる。雲水時代に福井の何やらいう寺で客僧をしておった。休日でみんな外へ遊びに出て行ったが、自分だけどこへも行くところがないから、三畳ばかりの小部屋へ入って坐禅をしておった。するとひょっこり飯焚き婆さんがその部屋へ何かを取りに来て障子を開けた。そのとたん、自分が坐禅しておる姿を見ると、婆さん、思わず立ったり坐ったりして、五体投地の三拝をしてしまった。その時、坐禅というものは、なんと尊いものだな、としみじみ感じた、と書いておられるが、威儀整然と坐禅した姿はそのまま仏の姿である。 When Hé was about to die, the only worthy person he recommended was Shēn. When Shēn succeeded Hé as the Chancellor of Hàn, in conducting affairs, he made no changes, but entirely followed the stipulations of Xiāo Hé.
The State of Qí was pacified and gathered, and he was greatly praised as a worthy minister.
In the second year of Emperor Huì, Xiāo Hé died. Cān heard of it, 將軍六人， [Six] generals. 大莫敖、 Dà Mò'áo, 郡守、 jùnshǒu, 司馬、 Sīmǎ, 侯、 hóu, and 御史 yùshǐ, each one person.
孝惠帝元年， Xiàohuì Dì yuánnián, (In) the first year of Emperor Xiaohui, 除諸侯相國法， chú zhūhóu xiàngguó fǎ, the law of the Chancellor of the vassal lords was abolished, 更以參為齊丞相。 gēng yǐ Shēn wèi Qí chéngxiàng. and Shēn was appointed as the Chancellor of Qí. 參之相齊， Shēn zhī xiàng Qí, When Shēn became the Chancellor of Qí, 齊七十城。 Qí qīshí chéng. Qí had seventy cities. 天下初定， tiānxià chū dìng, The world had just been settled, 悼惠王富於秦秋。 Dàohuì Wáng fù yú Qín qiū. and Dàohuì Wáng was richer than (during the late) Qín period. 參盡召長老諸生， Shēn jìn zhào zhǎnglǎo zhūshēng, Shēn summoned all the elders and scholars, 問所以安集百姓， wèn suǒyǐ ān jí bǎixìng, to ask how to pacify and gather the common people. 如齊故諸儒以百數， rú Qí gù zhūrú yǐ bǎishù, The former scholars of Qí numbered in the hundreds, 言人人殊， yán rén rén shū, and their opinions differed from person to person. 參未知所定。 Shēn wèi zhī suǒ dìng. Shēn did not know what to decide. 聞膠西有蓋公， wén Jiāoxī yǒu Gài Gōng, (He) heard that there was Gài Gōng in Jiaoxi, 善治黃老言， shàn zhì Huáng-Lǎo yán, who was good at governing with the teachings of Huang-Lao. 使人厚幣請之。 shǐ rén hòu bì qǐng zhī. (He) sent people with generous gifts to invite him. 既見蓋公， jì jiàn Gài Gōng, After meeting Gài Gōng, 蓋公為言治道貴清靜而民自定， Gài Gōng wèi yán zhì dào guì qīngjìng ér mín zì dìng, Gài Gōng said that the key to governance lies in tranquility and non-action, and the people will naturally settle down. 推此類具言之。 tuī cǐ lèi jù yán zhī. He fully explained this idea. 參於是避正堂， Shēn yúshì bì zhèngtáng, Thereupon, Shēn avoided the main hall, 舍蓋公焉。 shě Gài Gōng yān. and housed Gài Gōng (there). 其治要用黃老術， qí zhì yào yòng Huáng-Lǎo shù, The key to his governance was to use the Huang-Lao techniques, 故相齊九年， gù xiàng Qí jiǔ nián, therefore, for the nine years that he served as Chancellor of Qí, 齊國安集， Qí guó ān jí, the state of Qí was peaceful and well-ordered, 大稱賢相。 dà chēng xián xiàng. and he was greatly praised as a wise Chancellor.
惠帝二年， Huì Dì èr nián, (In) the second year of Emperor Hui, 蕭何卒。 Xiāo Hé zú. Xiao He died. 參聞之， Shēn wén zhī, When Shēn heard of it, 將軍六人， [Six] generals; 大莫敖、 Dà Mò'áo; 郡守、 jùnshǒu; 司馬、 Sīmǎ; 侯、 hóu; 御史各一人。 yùshǐ, one of each.
孝惠帝元年， In the first year of Emperor Xiàohuì; 除諸侯相國法， the laws regarding the Chancellors of the feudal lords were abolished; 更以參為齊丞相。 and Cān was appointed as the Chancellor of Qí. 參之相齊， When Cān was the Chancellor of Qí, 齊七十城。 Qí had seventy cities. 天下初定， The empire had just been stabilized, 悼惠王富於秦秋。 and King Dàohuì was wealthier than [even] Qín and Qiū. 參盡召長老諸生， Cān summoned all the elders and scholars, 問所以安集百姓， asking how to pacify and gather the people. 如齊故諸儒以百數， There were hundreds of former scholars of Qí, 言人人殊， and their opinions differed from person to person. 參未知所定。 Cān did not know what to decide. 聞膠西有蓋公， He heard that there was a Gài Gōng in Jiāoxī, 善治黃老言， who was skilled in the teachings of Huáng-Lǎo, 使人厚幣請之。 and he sent people with generous gifts to invite him. 既見蓋公， After meeting Gài Gōng, 蓋公為言治道貴清靜而民自定， Gài Gōng said that the key to governance is to value tranquility and the people will naturally be settled. 推此類具言之。 He elaborated on this principle in detail. 參於是避正堂， Cān then vacated the main hall, 舍蓋公焉。 and housed Gài Gōng there. 其治要用黃老術， His governance mainly employed the techniques of Huáng-Lǎo, 故相齊九年， therefore, in his nine years as Chancellor of Qí, 齊國安集， the state of Qí was peaceful and well-ordered, 大稱賢相。 and he was greatly praised as a wise Chancellor.
惠帝二年， In the second year of Emperor Xiàohuì, 蕭何卒。 Xiāo Hé died. 參聞之， When Cān heard of it, 將軍六人， [Six] generals. 大莫敖、 Dà Mò'áo, 郡守、 Jùnshǒu, 司馬、 Sīmǎ, 侯、 Hóu, and 御史 Yùshǐ, one of each.
Hán Xìn 韓信 was moved to become the King of Chǔ 楚, and Qí 齊 became a commandery. Cān 參 returned the seal of the Chancellor of Hàn 漢. Emperor Gāo 高帝 made his eldest son Féi 肥 the King of Qí 齊, and appointed Cān 參 as the Chancellor of Qí 齊. In the sixth year of Emperor Gāozǔ 高祖, he was granted the rank of Marquis, Hán Xìn 韓信 had already defeated Zhào 趙, and was acting as prime minister, attacking Qí 齊 in the east. Cān 參, as the Right Assistant Prime Minister, was subordinate to Hán Xìn 韓信, attacking and defeating the Qí 齊 army at Lìxià 歷下, and then taking Línzī 臨菑. In all, two years.
In the second year of Emperor Gaozu, he was appointed acting Left Chancellor, and entered Guanzhong to station troops. After a month or so, 赐食邑于 Níngqín. Cān, as general, led troops to besiege Zhāng Hán at Fèiqiū. As Commandant, he followed the King of Hàn from Línjìn Pass. Reaching Hénèi, he captured Xiūwǔ, crossed Wéijīn, Destroyed the Tàishǐ (泰史, Grand Scribe's records)
Xiàng Yǔ (項羽) arrived and made Pèi Gōng (沛公), Liú Bāng, the King of Hàn (漢王). The King of Hàn enfeoffed Shēn (參) as the Marquis of Jiànchéng (建成侯). "Biography Five: Sūnzǐ and Wú Qǐ"
Sūnzǐ Wǔ was a man of Qí. He presented his art of war to Hélǘ, King of Wú. Hélǘ said: "I have completely read your thirteen chapters.
Can we try drilling troops in a small test?" He replied: "Yes." Hélǘ said: "Can we try it with women?" He said: "Yes." Thereupon he permitted it, and brought out beautiful women from the palace, obtaining one hundred and eighty people. Sūnzǐ divided them into two teams. He said: "Yes." Sūnzǐ said: "If the rules are not clear, and the orders are not thoroughly explained, "The troops are already well-ordered, the King can try coming down to observe them, use them as the King wishes, even plunging into water and fire is possible." The King of Wú said: "General, rest and return to your quarters, "Now that the troops are fully trained and disciplined, Your Majesty may wish to come down and observe them. You may command them as you desire, and they will even plunge into water and fire if necessary." Wú Wáng said: "General, you may rest and return to your quarters. I have no desire to come down and observe." Sūn Zǐ said: "The king merely appreciates my words, but cannot apply their substance." Thereupon, Hélǘ realized Sūn Zǐ's ability to command troops, and finally appointed him as general. He then westward defeated the powerful Chǔ, entered Yǐng, and to the north, awed Qí and Jìn, making his name known among the feudal lords. Sūn Zǐ played a significant role in this.
After Sūn Wǔ died, more than a hundred years later, there was Sūn Bìn. Bìn was born between Ā and Juàn, and Bìn was also a descendant of Sūn Wǔ. Sūn Bìn once studied military strategy with Páng Juān. After Páng Juān served Wèi, he became a general for King Huì, but believing that his abilities were inferior to Sūn Bìn, he secretly sent for Sūn Bìn. When Bìn arrived, Páng Juān, fearing that he was more talented than himself, became jealous of him. He then used the law to cut off both of his feet and tattooed his face, intending to keep him hidden from view.
When an envoy from Qí went to Liáng, Páng Juān, fearing that he was more capable than himself, resented him, and then used legal punishment to cut off both his feet and tattoo his face, wanting to hide him and not let him be seen.
A Qí envoy came to Liáng, Páng Juān 龐涓, fearing that he (Sūn Bìn 孫臏) was more capable than himself, envied him. He then used the law to inflict punishment, cutting off both of his feet and tattooing his face, wanting to hide him away and not let him be seen.
When an envoy from Qí 齊 went to Liáng 梁, Sūn Bìn 孫臏, as a criminal, secretly met with him and persuaded the Qí 齊 envoy. The Qí 齊 envoy considered him remarkable and secretly took him to Qí 齊. The Qí 齊 general Tián Jì 田忌 treated him well and lodged him as a guest. Tián Jì 田忌 frequently raced horses with the various noble sons of Qí 齊, betting heavily. Sūnzǐ 孫子 saw that the horses' feet were not very far apart (in quality), and that the horses had upper, middle, and lower classes. Thereupon, Sūnzǐ 孫子 said to Tián Jì 田忌, "Your Lordship, feel free to bet heavily; I can ensure that you win." Tián Jì 田忌 believed him, and raced with the King and the various noble sons, betting a thousand gold pieces. When they were about to begin, Sūnzǐ 孫子 said, "Now, use your lower-class horse against their upper-class horse, use your upper-class horse against their middle-class horse, and use your middle-class horse against their lower-class horse." After they had raced all three classes, Tián Jì 田忌 lost one race but won two, and ultimately won a thousand gold pieces from the King. Thereupon, Jì 忌 presented Sūnzǐ 孫子 to King Wēi 威王. King Wēi 威王 asked him about military strategy, and eventually made him his teacher.
Later, Wèi 魏 attacked Zhào 趙. Zhào 趙 was in a critical situation. Thereupon, Jì 忌 recommended Sūnzi 孫子 to King Wēi 威 of Qí 齊. King Wēi 威 asked him about military strategy, and subsequently appointed him as his teacher.

Ancient scholars and past students, in their written works and chapters, all discussed [this], but none could definitively settle [the matter].
Shì Shuò of Zhōu believed that human nature has both good and evil. If one elevates a person's good nature, nurtures and develops it, then goodness will grow. If their nature is evil, nurture and develop it, then evil will grow. If this is so, then emotion and nature each have yin and yang; good and evil depend on what is nurtured. Therefore, Shì Zǐ composed the "Yǎng Shū" (Nurturing Book) in one chapter. Mì Zǐjiàn, Qīdiāo Kāi, and the disciples of Gōngsūn Nízǐ, also discussed emotion and nature, with opinions similar to and differing from those of Shì Zǐ, all saying that nature has both good and evil.

The "Chapter on the Nature of Things". The Confucians argue, saying: "Heaven and Earth deliberately created humans." This statement is absurd.
When Heaven and Earth combine their qi, humans are spontaneously produced by chance; it is like when husband and wife combine their qi, the child is spontaneously produced. When husband and wife combine their qi, it is not that they intentionally want to have a child at that time; rather, their emotions and desires move them to combine, and combining results in the birth of a child. Furthermore, husband and wife do not deliberately create a child, thus we know that Heaven and Earth do not deliberately create humans. Therefore, humans are born from Heaven and Earth, just as fish are in a pond, or lice are on a person; they are born due to qi, and their kinds reproduce each other. The myriad things that are born between Heaven and Earth are all a single reality.

かくして、お互いの修行がだんだん出来てくると、「道高ければ魔盛んにして」だ。修行のできるほど、いろいろな魔障が起こってくる。「逆順万端なり」で、魔障にも順魔と逆魔とがある。 かくして、お互いの修行がだんだん出来てくると、「道高ければ魔盛んにして」だ。修行のできるほど、いろいろな魔障が起こってくる。「逆順万端なり」で、魔障にも順魔と逆魔とがある。 順魔というのは、我々の感情や意欲にうまく順応して、巧みに道の妨げをする魔障である。逆魔というのは、我々の意志や感情に逆らって、道心を破壊させる魔障である。僧堂でも古参になると、あっちで可愛いがられ、こっちでもてはやされ、将来はどんな立派な老師になるじゃろう、などと期待されておるうちに、つい酒を呑むことだけを覚えて修行を放擲してしまうような雲水が出てくる。こういうのを順魔という。まことに惜しいことだが仕方がない。 To sit carrying a woman on one's back, is to say the woman is on one's back. If Duke Huán were to use a woman to remove the hereditary disease, The officials of the Ministry of Rites should not have one foot; it's like a guard who cuts off his foot, which is not worthy of esteem. Kǒng Jiǎ could not obtain a noble son; Bó Yí could not yield to Kuí. He was the Zōngzhèng 宗正 (Director of the Imperial Clan) of the Hàn 漢 dynasty. His foot was cut off. The foot was not in its proper state. Moreover, a one-footed person, what use is he for walking? Xiàhòu Kǒngjiǎ 夏后孔甲 hunted at Dōngyáng Bìshān 東陽萯山. The sky rained, dark and gloomy. He entered a commoner's house. The master of the house was just then delivering a child. Someone said, "If it comes later, this child will surely be noble." Someone said, "If it cannot overcome [the difficulty of birth], this child will surely be base." Kǒngjiǎ 孔甲 said, "If it is my child, who can make him base?" Thereupon he took [the child] and brought him home. [He was] splitting rafters, [and an] axe cut off his foot. In the end, he became a watchman. Kǒngjiǎ's 孔甲 desire to ennoble the child, he had ample power for it; the foot being cut off was not suitable, therefore he became a watchman. Now, Kuí 夔 has one foot, without the ability to run and walk, sitting and tuning music, that is acceptable. The office of the Minister of Rites (秩宗 zhīzōng), is not suitable for one foot, it's like a watchman having his foot cut off, it is impossible to make him noble. Kǒngjiǎ 孔甲 could not ennoble the child, Bó Yí 伯夷 could not yield [his position] to Kuí 夔. Hàn's Zōngzhèng also. [He] cut off a foot. A foot is not in its proper state. "Commentary Records" states: The virtue of Master Wèi, was that he was benevolent and kind to subordinates, and extended it even to birds and beasts. Once, while drinking with guests, a hawk attacked a dove. The dove fled, and went around under Master's table. The hawk pursued and attacked, killing it in front of Master. Master felt ashamed of this, and immediately had many nets set, catching dozens of hawks. He rebuked them for the crime of attacking the dove. The hawks that attacked the dove, lowered their heads, not daring to look up. Master then killed them.
The world praised him, saying: "Master Wèi avenged the dove." This is a false statement.
For a hawk is a creature; its feelings and heart are different, and its sounds and language are unintelligible. Even a sage cannot make birds and beasts behave according to principles of righteousness. What sort of person is Master? 鳥為鸇者 number in the millions. Once they strike a dove and it flies away, how can you get it back? If one can lower its head and blame itself, then that is a holy bird.
